# QuickKit

> Everyday tools. One command away.

QuickKit is a privacy-conscious, local-first collection of everyday browser utilities. All calculations run entirely in the user's browser — no account, no application backend, no database, no analytics. The production build is a static export of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript served from https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev.

Product characteristics:
- Local-first: every calculation runs in the browser
- Offline-capable: installable as a PWA with a service worker for offline use
- No account, no backend, no database
- No analytics or tracking
- Quick Command: a global deterministic command bar (Ctrl/Cmd+K) that runs the same engines as the graphical tools

Site URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev
Repository: https://github.com/quickkit/quickkit
License: MIT (https://opensource.org/license/mit)
Author: Asaad

## Tools

QuickKit contains exactly eight tools:

1. Unit Converter
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/unit-converter
   Length, mass, temperature, speed, area, and digital storage.

2. Percentage & Money
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/percentage
   Percent of, discounts, tips, and percentage change.

3. QR Generator
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/qr
   Generate QR codes locally for text and URLs.

4. Password & PIN
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/password
   Cryptographically secure passwords and PINs, never saved.

5. Date Calculator
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/date
   Difference between dates, add and subtract durations.

6. Text Tools
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/text
   Word, character, and line counts; case and whitespace fixes.

7. Random Picker
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/random
   Random integers, choices, coin flips, and dice.

8. Color Converter
   URL: https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/tools/color
   HEX, RGB, HSL — bidirectional, with a live preview.

## Important Pages

- Guide (https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/guide): QuickKit Quick Command reference — supported commands, examples, tool capabilities, keyboard shortcut, local/private processing.
- About (https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/about): what QuickKit is, local-first philosophy, offline capability, open-source nature, MIT license, and the developer.
- Privacy (https://quickkit-59o.pages.dev/privacy): accurate privacy practices — no account, no backend, no database, calculations happen locally, sensitive transient data is not durably persisted.

## Privacy / Runtime Characteristics

- All calculations run locally in the browser
- Sensitive transient data (generated passwords, PINs, QR payloads, raw text content, random choice lists) is held only in memory and is never durably persisted
- Durable local storage is limited to: theme preference, favorites (tool identities only), Recent Tools (tool identities only, never inputs or results), and haptics preference
- No operation/calculation history feature exists
- Offline/PWA: a service worker caches the application shell and tool routes for offline use; no push notifications
